conviction_note: The searches turned up no company-level number the market lacks. The two peer prints from today (GS AWM: record AUS, $97bn long-term inflows, management fees +7% QoQ; JPM firmwide asset-management fees +4% QoQ) and record Q3 ETF industry flows support base fees near the $6.02bn consensus. Against that sit HLEND's 11.5% Q3 redemption requests and the September bond/FX drawdown hitting period-end AUM. The 4-of-4 up reaction history and the stock lagging SPY by 4 points since July give a slight upward lean, so p_up is 55 on an abs move of 4.8 (+0.48 scaled). The findings sum to +0.6; the two measurements agree in sign and are about the same size.

findings.finding: HPS Corporate Lending Fund (HLEND), BlackRock's flagship non-traded private-credit BDC, received Q3 2026 repurchase requests of about 11.5% of shares. That is up from 9.3% in Q1, when it first gated to 5% and BLK fell about 8%. A third-party secondary tender was launched at $20.17, a 17.5% discount to NAV. The fund's own Q3 offer covers about 5% of shares, plus an optional 2%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The first HLEND gate in March 2026 took BLK down 7-8% intraday (https://alternativecreditinvestor.com/2026/03/06/blackrock-shares-slide-after-26bn-private-credit-fund-gates-withdrawals/). The baseline's four prints were all up, including Q2 2026, after the gate.
findings.resolves_by: 2026-10-14 — the release's private-markets flows and the call's commentary on private wealth credit
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: public since 2026-09-24 and BLK has lagged SPY by about 4 points since July. What may not be priced is how the call frames private-wealth fundraising and HLEND net flows. Had the market fully priced a deterioration, the put skew would be bid rather than call-leaning (-1.19).
findings.independence: The fund's own SC TO-I for the Q3 offer (about 5% of shares, NAV $24.42 at 2026-06-30, pro-rata if oversubscribed): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001838126/000162828026055335/a2exa1ii-offertopurchaseq3.htm. Same vehicle, different document. HLEND is a small slice of $15.3tn AUM; the rest of the company (iShares, base fees) is not touched by this.

findings.finding: Goldman Sachs' Q3 2026 release (today, 2026-10-13) shows AWM management fees +7% QoQ on higher average AUS, long-term net inflows of $97bn, net market depreciation of -$27bn on $4.04tn (-0.7%), and incentive fees of $587m (+424% QoQ). JPMorgan's firmwide asset-management fees rose 4% QoQ. Both point to average-AUM-driven fee growth that supports BLK's +5% QoQ base-fee consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BLK's base-fee and flow beats preceded all four up reactions in the baseline (+3.39, +5.93, +3.02, +6.63). Q2 2026: $192bn net inflows and 8% organic base fee growth, +6.63%.
findings.why_not_priced: These are peer prints published after BLK last spoke, and the line consensus (Zacks) predates them. BLK's sealed spot at 17:08 UTC has had only one session to absorb them. If the market had read them through, BLK would have outperformed other financials today; the baseline 5-day run-up is -0.37%.
findings.independence: JPM 3Q26 supplement, firmwide asset-management fees $5,897m against $5,658m (+4%): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000019617/000162828026065582/a3q26erfex992supplement.htm. A different company and a different document.

findings.finding: US ETF industry inflows hit a record $771bn in Q3 2026 (Citadel Securities data, through 2026-09-29) against $560bn in Q2. FactSet shows September at $140.9bn after $182.6bn in August, and YTD above $1.5tn. iShares holds about 32% of US ETF assets, so flows into BLK's highest-volume product line look at least as strong as Q2's $178bn of ETF inflows.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Record ETF flows in Q2 2026 ($178bn into iShares ETFs) went with a +6.63% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Industry ETF flows are tracked daily by the sell-side, so this is largely priced. What is not observable is iShares' Q3 share. The September slowdown and Invesco's -$1.1bn long-term September outflow keep this small.
findings.independence: FactSet's September 2026 US ETF summary ($140.9bn in September, $182.6bn in August, $1.5tn YTD): https://insight.factset.com/u.s.-etf-monthly-summary-september-2026-results. Counter-evidence: Invesco's September AUM release (https://finviz.com/news/400763/invesco-ltd-announces-september-30-2026-assets-under-management). This is a proxy, not BLK's own number.

findings.finding: A September rates shock likely cut period-end AUM: the 10-year Treasury rose 52bp to about 5.27% around the Fed's first hike since 2023 on 2026-09-16, the dollar rose, and Q3 small caps fell 7.2%. Peers marked down: GS net market depreciation -$27bn (-0.7%), and Invesco's September markets -$16bn and FX -$2.7bn. BLK's end-Q3 AUM is therefore likely around $15.4-15.5tn against the single-source $15.67tn consensus, which lowers the Q4 base-fee entry run rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline isolates period-end AUM; all four prints rose on flows and EPS beats.
findings.why_not_priced: The rates move is public and BLK is 10.6% off its high, so most of it is priced. The AUM consensus is one Zacks number, and any stale model above $15.6tn would be revised on the print. The finding is capped small because that bar is single-source.
findings.independence: Invesco's September 2026 AUM release (market -$16bn, FX -$2.7bn): https://finviz.com/news/400763/invesco-ltd-announces-september-30-2026-assets-under-management. Q3 index returns: https://novelinvestor.com/2026-q3-returns/. The GS document is shared with finding 2, but this finding reads the market-depreciation line, not the fee or flow lines.

findings.finding: Reaction function and positioning favour upside on a clean print. baseline_tension: The modest positive lean agrees with the slightly call-bid skew and the balanced put/call OI. It cuts mildly against the stock's 4-point lag versus SPY since July, which partly reflects the HLEND and rates concerns already in the price.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): HLEND is a small slice of AUM and the rest of the company is unaffected, so -0.6 became -0.4.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the AUM consensus is Zacks-only, so the period-end AUM finding was capped from -0.4 to -0.3.
Lesson 5 (narrow proxy vs broader series): the industry ETF flow proxy is partly contradicted by the September slowdown and Invesco's outflow, so +0.4 became +0.3.
What has worked (a peer print after the company last spoke): left the GS/JPM finding at +0.5.
